boundary_condition: Apply only to hotel/lodging quality filters; if the request explicitly states a stricter rating threshold such as 4 or 4.5 stars, use that stricter threshold for that search.
condition: When searching for hotels or lodging and no trip-specific rating target has been stated.
default_action: Exclude hotels below 3 stars; among eligible hotels, show 4-star-or-higher and strong-review properties first.
exception_condition: If no 3-star-or-better hotel satisfies required dates, location, or required amenities, ask before relaxing the rating floor and showing lower-rated options.
name: Prefers midscale-or-better, highly rated hotels
preference_value: minimum 3-star-or-better hotels, with 4-star or highly reviewed options preferred
rationale: Across independent hotel-search dialogues, speakers repeatedly use ratings as a quality gate: some ask for at least 4 stars or 4.5 stars, one asks generally for high star ratings and good reviews, and one gives a lower floor of at least 3 stars. A coherent synthetic default supported by all examples is to avoid low-rated hotels by default while prioritizing higher-rated options when available, rather than treating any single trip's 4-star or 4.5-star threshold as universal.
